title: Declarative retention policies (foundational)
description: Retention rules are declared as data, not code: each rule names a data class, a retention period, and an action on expiry such as delete or anonymize. Declared policies can be reviewed and versioned like any other configuration. The controller interprets them uniformly, so behavior is consistent across every database it governs. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Expiry enforcement sweep (foundational)
description: The sweep compares each item's age against its class policy and executes the declared action on expired items. Items are processed oldest-first so the sweep makes steady progress even if interrupted. Every action is idempotent: re-running the sweep on an already-processed item changes nothing. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
from datetime import date
items = [('q1', 'query-log', date(2026, 6, 1)), ('f1', 'finding', date(2026, 6, 1))]
pol = {'query-log': 90, 'finding': 365}
today = date(2026, 10, 21)
for iid, cls, born in items:
    expired = (today - born).days > pol[cls]
    print(iid, 'EXPIRED -> delete' if expired else 'keep')

title: Privacy purge on request (foundational)
description: A deletion request triggers a targeted purge: every item tagged with the requester's identifier is located via the index and removed, including from backups within the backup retention window. The purge is verified by re-querying for the identifier afterward and confirming zero hits. Verification output is kept as proof of compliance. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
store = [{'id': 'a', 'user': 'u7'}, {'id': 'b', 'user': 'u9'}, {'id': 'c', 'user': 'u7'}]
store = [r for r in store if r['user'] != 'u7']
print('remaining:', [r['id'] for r in store])
print('verify zero hits for u7:', not any(r['user'] == 'u7' for r in store))

title: Legal hold override (foundational)
description: A legal hold flag on an item suspends all expiry and purge actions for that item until the hold is explicitly released. Holds override every policy, including privacy purges, and each hold records who placed it and why. The controller refuses to delete held items even when every other rule says to, because the hold represents a higher authority. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Forgetting and Retention Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Deletion audit trail (foundational)
description: Every deletion writes an audit entry: what was removed, which rule fired, when, and by which sweep. The trail itself is append-only and exempt from expiry, so the history of forgetting is never forgotten. Auditors use this trail to prove that retention rules were actually enforced. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
trail = []
def delete(iid, rule):
    trail.append({'id': iid, 'rule': rule, 'when': '2026-10-21'})
delete('q1', 'query-log 90-day expiry')
print('audit trail:', trail)
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Forgetting and Retention Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
